name: Model Context Protocol (MCP)
certifications: No official MCP certification; assessed by working servers and clients, test suites and a security review
Optional: vendor courses on building MCP servers
tools: An MCP host such as Claude Desktop or VS Code
OAuth 2.1 authorization server such as Keycloak

beginner.summary: For developers who connect AI assistants and agents to tools and data. Covers what MCP is, hosts, clients and servers, JSON-RPC messages, setting up the SDKs and MCP Inspector, using existing servers in AI hosts, building tool servers in Python and TypeScript, tool design and schemas, structured output and errors, resources and prompts, the stdio and Streamable HTTP transports, testing, wrapping REST APIs and databases, asking users for input with multi round-trip requests, building a simple client, security essentials and packaging servers, following the 2026-07-28 specification.
prerequisites: Has called a REST API and used an AI assistant
outcomes: Explain how MCP hosts, clients and servers work together
Build MCP servers in Python and TypeScript with well-designed tools, resources and prompts
Run servers over stdio and Streamable HTTP and test them with MCP Inspector
Apply security essentials such as least privilege and protection against prompt injection

days.topic: MCP Overview: Hosts, Clients and Servers
subtopics: The problem MCP solves: one way to connect models to tools and data
MCP compared with plain function calling
Where MCP is used: assistants, IDEs and agents
The 2026-07-28 revision in brief: a stateless core
SDKs: TypeScript, Python, Go and C#
Course project overview: an MCP server for a company's order system

days.deliverable: Capability list and a role diagram
checks: Both servers appear in the host with their capabilities
A tool call completes and its result appears in the conversation
The diagram shows host, client and server roles correctly

subtopics: Methods such as tools/list and tools/call

intermediate.summary: For developers who build MCP servers and now run them remotely for teams. Covers stateless server design with explicit handles, protocol versions and discovery, OAuth 2.1 authorization, client ID metadata documents and issuer validation, the Tasks extension for long-running work, subscriptions, cacheable lists, header-based routing and gateways, deployment, observability, evaluating tool use, MCP in agent frameworks, composing many servers, Go and C# SDKs, the MCP Apps extension, migrating from earlier versions, versioning tools, conformance testing and load testing.
prerequisites: Has built MCP servers with tools, resources and prompts
Comfortable with HTTP, JSON and one of Python or TypeScript
Understands OAuth at a high level
outcomes: Design stateless remote servers that scale and keep state in explicit handles
Secure remote servers with OAuth 2.1 and current authorization rules
Use extensions, subscriptions, caching and gateways in production
Deploy, observe, evaluate and version servers used by agents and teams

advanced.summary: For architects, platform engineers and security leads who run MCP across an organisation. Covers enterprise MCP architecture, enterprise managed authorization, threat modelling, defending against injection through tool results, sandboxing, multi-tenant servers, governance of third-party servers, data protection and audit, building hosts and clients, writing extensions, large tool catalogues, human oversight, scaling, cost and token efficiency, reliability, platform operations, contributing to the specification, interoperability with other agent protocols and troubleshooting.
prerequisites: Has deployed and secured remote MCP servers
Understands OAuth, identity and API gateways
Responsible for AI platforms, integration or security
outcomes: Design an enterprise MCP platform with registries, gateways, identity and policy
Threat-model and defend MCP deployments, including injection and supply chain risks
Build hosts, clients and extensions and keep large tool catalogues usable
Operate MCP at scale with governance, audit and reliability
